contributions.statement: Accept an agent artifact only if every acceptance obligation passes, not on the share of checks passed, because long-context runs still satisfied about 93% of checks while strict success fell to 3/10.
contributions.evidence: §5.3.1: 92.1-93.8% check satisfaction in long conditions; failures concentrated on a few recurrent array/cardinality rules. One task, one main model, n=10.

contributions.statement: At the completion step, restate the full frozen acceptance criteria from the spec instead of a generic 'double-check your work' prompt, which passed 10/10 vs 5/10 in this audit task.
contributions.evidence: Table 7: 240/240 vs 234/240 checks, p=0.0325, single n=10 comparison. Audit: the restated list equals the scoring rubric, so it shows the agent satisfies criteria it is reminded of, not that unlisted quality improves.

contributions.statement: Do not rely on context compaction to carry exact contracts (enum lists, field mappings) into a delegated sub-agent; have it re-read them from committed files.
contributions.evidence: §5.6.1: one valid mechanism run in which the worker reported losing an opaque 256-entry contract after native compaction; self-reported, raw receipt lost.

reason: Small and exploratory, but it gives two directly usable gate rules for spec-driven work (strict per-obligation acceptance; restate frozen criteria at completion). The compaction point is a single-run hypothesis.
